title: Execution of the Idolaters

questions.question: In Ezekiel's vision, whom did the Lord call out to with a loud voice in his hearing?
options: The executioners of the city
The watchmen of the walls
The angels of death
The armies of the north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:1 (ESV): "Then he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying, 'Bring near the executioners of the city, each with his destroying weapon in his hand.'"

questions.question: From what direction did the six men come, each with his weapon for slaughter in his hand?
options: From the direction of the upper gate, which faces north
From the eastern gate
From the southern gate of the court
From the wilderness to the west
questions.correctAnswer: From the direction of the upper gate, which faces north
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 (ESV): "And behold, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for slaughter in his hand,"

questions.question: Who was among the six men, clothed in linen?
options: A man with a writing case at his waist
A high priest with a breastplate
An angel holding a measuring line
A warrior with a golden shield
questions.correctAnswer: A man with a writing case at his waist
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 (ESV): "and with them was a man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his waist."

questions.question: Where did the six men and the man clothed in linen go and stand?
options: Beside the bronze altar
Inside the Holy of Holies
At the entrance of the city
On the Mount of Olives
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:2 (ESV): "And they went in and stood beside the bronze altar."

questions.question: What movement did the glory of the God of Israel make before speaking to the man clothed in linen?
options: It went up from the cherub on which it rested to the threshold of the house
It departed from the city and went to the mountain
It filled the temple with smoke
It ascended into the clouds
questions.correctAnswer: It went up from the cherub on which it rested to the threshold of the house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:3 (ESV): "Now the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the cherub on which it rested to the threshold of the house."

questions.question: What did God tell the man clothed in linen to do?
options: "Pass through the city... and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it."
"Write down the names of all the elders who worship idols."
"Take burning coals and scatter them over the city."
"Open the gates for the Chaldeans."
questions.correctAnswer: "Pass through the city... and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:4 (ESV): "Pass through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it."

questions.question: What command did God give to the other six men?
options: "Pass through the city after him, and strike. Your eye shall not spare, and you shall show no pity."
"Wait at the gates until he returns."
"Destroy only the high places and the altars."
"Capture the wicked and bind them in chains."
questions.correctAnswer: "Pass through the city after him, and strike. Your eye shall not spare, and you shall show no pity."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:5 (ESV): "And to the others he said in my hearing, 'Pass through the city after him, and strike. Your eye shall not spare, and you shall show no pity.'"

questions.question: Who were the men instructed to strike and destroy?
options: Old men outright, young men and maidens, little children and women
Only the seventy elders
Only the men with weapons
Only the priests of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Old men outright, young men and maidens, little children and women
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 (ESV): "Kill old men outright, young men and maidens, little children and women,"

questions.question: Who were the executioners forbidden to touch?
options: Anyone on whom is the mark
Anyone taking refuge in the temple
Anyone who wept for Tammuz
Anyone claiming to be a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Anyone on whom is the mark
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 (ESV): "but touch no one on whom is the mark."

questions.question: Where were the executioners commanded to begin their slaughter?
options: At my sanctuary
At the king's palace
At the city walls
In the valley of Hinnom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:6 (ESV): "And begin at my sanctuary. So they began with the elders who were before the house."

questions.question: What did God tell them to do to the temple courts before going out into the city?
options: Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain
Wash the courts with water
Burn the doors with fire
Lock the gates forever
questions.correctAnswer: Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:7 (ESV): "And he said to them, 'Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain. Go out.' So they went out and struck in the city."

questions.question: When Ezekiel was left alone and saw the slaughter, what did he do?
options: He fell on his face and cried out, "Ah, Lord God! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel...?"
He ran to hide in the mountains
He rejoiced that the idolaters were destroyed
He took up a weapon to fight the executioners
questions.correctAnswer: He fell on his face and cried out, "Ah, Lord God! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel...?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:8 (ESV): "And while they were striking, and I was left alone, I fell upon my face, and cried, 'Ah, Lord God! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel in the outpouring of your wrath on Jerusalem?'"

questions.question: What reasoning did God give Ezekiel for His unsparing wrath?
options: "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of blood, and the city full of injustice."
"They have formed an alliance with Egypt against me." "They did not observe the Sabbath day."
"They murdered the prophets I sent."
questions.correctAnswer: "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of blood, and the city full of injustice."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of blood, and the city full of injustice.'"

questions.question: What did the people say in their hearts that led to this injustice?
options: "The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord does not see."
"The gods of Babylon are stronger than Yahweh."
"We will bring peace through our own power."
"The temple will protect us no matter what we do."
questions.correctAnswer: "The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord does not see."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:9 (ESV): "For they say, 'The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord does not see.'"

questions.question: At the end of the chapter, what report did the man clothed in linen with the writing case bring back?
options: "I have done as you commanded me."
"The city is destroyed."
"No one was found with the mark."
"The people have repented."
questions.correctAnswer: "I have done as you commanded me."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 9:11 (ESV): "And behold, the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his waist, brought back word, saying, 'I have done as you commanded me.'"

key_verse_text: And the Lord said to him, "Pass through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it."
